items.title: Photos: First look at J&J’s Ottava surgical robot
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson MedTech's Ottava surgical robot features four robotic arms that come out from underneath the operating table, designed to save space in the OR by taking up 30-50% less room than traditional boom-and-cart systems. The system is equipped with a two-in-one needle driver and patented scissor design, aiming to reduce inadvertent suture cuts and dull scissors. Surgeons can control the instruments from an ergonomic console where they maintain natural posture and access to the full workspace.
items.audio_script:
From The Robot Report, "Photos: First look at J&J’s Ottava surgical robot", Johnson & Johnson MedTech has unveiled its latest innovation in robotic surgery technology. According to the company's announcements, Ottava is a minimally invasive surgical system featuring four robotic arms that emerge from underneath the operating table, designed to save space by occupying 30-50% less room than traditional systems. The system boasts a two-in-one needle driver and patented scissor design aimed at reducing inadvertent suture cuts and dull scissors. Surgeons can control instruments from an ergonomic console while maintaining natural posture and accessing the full workspace. This new technology promises to enhance surgical precision, efficiency, and patient outcomes.

The Ottava system is the result of significant advancements in robotic surgery engineering, with the goal of providing surgeons with increased flexibility, dexterity, and control during complex procedures. The innovative design allows for more precise dissection and suturing, potentially leading to better wound closure rates and reduced complications. As the medical technology industry continues to evolve, the Ottava system represents a significant step forward in robotic surgery capabilities.

The introduction of Ottava marks an exciting development in the AI-driven surgical tools sector, as it further emphasizes the role of robotics in enhancing human surgical capabilities. With its cutting-edge features and streamlined design, surgeons can now access more precise control over intricate procedures, paving the way for improved patient care.
